O R D E R
The proceedings taken under Section 138 of the Negotiable
Instruments Act, 1881 with respect to dishonor of cheque amounting
to Rs.12,60,000/- ended in a conviction of the accused, who is the
petitioner  herein.  This Court by  order  dated  05.12.2025 directed
deposit of Rs.15,60,000/-.
2. We referred the parties to mediation and when the matter was
posted today, we are told that the matter has been settled and
parties have agreed to settle the issue on payment of Rs.15,60,000/-
by the petitioner to the respondent. The settlement agreement is
produced before this Court and the operative portion is extracted
hereunder:
xxx                                    xxx                                xxx
7. Whereas it has mutually been decided between both the
parties that the amount already deposited by the First Party an
amount of Rs. 15,60,000/- in the SLP (CRL) No. 21281/2025,
before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India vide demand draft
no.  082252  dated  09.12.2025,  in  the  name  of  Registrar
General, Supreme Court of India, the said amount alongwith
the interest incurred till date shall be released in favour of
Second party and in that eventuality First party shall have no

## Page 414

objection. Further it has also been decided between both the
parties  that  Second  party  shall  have  no  objection  if  the
judgment of conviction dated 11.09.2024 passed by Ld. CJM
Shimla, in complaint CIS Registration No. 1193/2022 titled as
Ramesh Chauhan v/s Joginder Singh Chauhan and affirmed by
the  Ld.  Additional  Sessions  Judge  (CBI  Court)  Shimla,  in
Criminal  Appeal  No.  96-S/10  of  2024  vide  judgment  dated
15.03.2025, and further affirmed by the Hon'ble High Court of
HP in Criminal Revision Petition No. 209/2025 vide judgment
dated 14.05.2025, will be quash and set aside by the Hon'ble
Supreme Court of India.
xxx                                    xxx                                xxx
3. The said amount has been deposited in the Registry of this
Court. We direct the Registry to disburse the amount together with
any  interest  accrued  to  the  respondent/complainant  on  proper
verification.
4. In terms of the settlement, we set aside the impugned order
and the orders of the First Appellate Court and the Trial Court. The
conviction of the petitioner is set aside.
5. The petition shall stand disposed of on the above observations.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand rejected.

## Page 479

from  the  mother’s  residence  at  Bengaluru,  Karnataka  on

house/residence of the petitioner at Bengaluru.

before 14.10.2026 before this Court.
4. It is made clear that the breach of undertaking by any
party, will result in serious consequence.
5. Both parties to furnish the their respective residential
addresses to each other,  to facilitate pick up and drop back
of the children.
6. We also make it clear that during the period of stay with
the father, the mother will have video call access to the
children every day.
7. Both the learned Senior Counsel for the parties also
report that they had discussing a shared parenting arrangement
for the long term also and that is getting firmed up. The
petitioner has furnished a draft proposal and that is under
consideration at the hands of the respondent.

progress to conclude the trial is achieved within one year next from date of
communication of this order to the trial court despite full cooperation extended
by the petitioner for concluding the trial, he shall be at liberty to renew his
prayer for bail before the jurisdictional court.

Delay condoned.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material
placed on record.
3. Having regard to the nature and gravity of the allegations, we
are not inclined to grant bail to the petitioner.
4. However, keeping in view the fact that the petitioner is in
custody for nearly four years and ten months, the Trial Court is
directed to expedite the trial and shall try to conclude the same

## Page 703

2
preferably  within  a  period  of  one  year  from  the  date  of
presentation of a copy of this order. 
5. It goes without saying that the prosecution as well as the
defence shall co-operate with the trial. In case, for no fault
attributable to the petitioner, the trial is not concluded within
the aforesaid period, the petitioner would be at liberty to renew
his prayer for bail.
6. The  Special  Leave  Petition  is  dismissed  with  the  above
observations.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
